points.description: States that a CNN contains a convolutional layer whose kernels (filters) convolve/slide over the input image. Accept equivalent wording such as 'filters scan the image' or 'convolution operation over the input'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if the answer mentions a convolutional layer but gives no kernel/filter or convolution-over-input detail, or mentions kernels/convolving without identifying the convolutional layer.

levels.says: Mentions a convolutional layer only, or mentions kernels/convolving over the input without naming the convolutional layer.

points.description: States that the CNN includes an activation layer, specifically ReLU (or a nonlinear activation). Accept 'ReLU layer' or 'activation function such as ReLU'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if an activation layer is mentioned but ReLU/nonlinear activation is not specified.

levels.says: Mentions an activation layer but does not name ReLU or a nonlinear activation.

points.description: States that the CNN includes a pooling layer, such as max pooling or average pooling. Accept 'pooling layer' with either max or average named.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if pooling is mentioned without specifying max or average pooling.

levels.says: Mentions a pooling layer but does not specify max or average pooling.

points.description: States that the CNN has one or more fully connected layers followed by a softmax layer. Accept equivalent wording such as 'dense layers ending in softmax'.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if fully connected/dense layers are mentioned without softmax, or softmax is mentioned without fully connected layers.

levels.says: Mentions fully connected/dense layers without softmax, or softmax without fully connected layers.

rubric.notes: Full marks require the convolutional layer with kernels convolving over the input image, plus mention of an activation layer (ReLU), a pooling layer (max or average), and fully connected layer(s) followed by softmax. Part marks are given for incomplete layer descriptions, such as naming a layer without its key detail or omitting some of the listed layer types. No marks are given for answers that do not describe CNN layers or give unrelated neural-network components.
